_: The claims Knos can prove on NEAR testnet: each from a real paper (its words quoted from its abstract), with its locked test in near/agents/job/ and its two agents' code in near/agents/ (hyperloglog) or near/agents/solutions/. The test's sha256 is the criteria hash every job for the claim is opened with. Read by the site (scripts/site_pages.py) and the hosted server (apps/wanted/knos_wanted/near_live.py).

claims.name: hyperloglog
claims.plain: HyperLogLog counts 30,000 different visitors within 10% using at most 1.5 kilobytes of memory.
claims.paper: HyperLogLog: the analysis of a near-optimal cardinality estimation algorithm
claims.quote: For instance, the new algorithm makes it possible to estimate cardinalities well beyond 10^9 with a typical accuracy of 2% while using a memory of only 1.5 kilobytes.
claims.locked: count 30,000 visitors within 10%, in at most 1.5 kilobytes
claims.question: Does HyperLogLog count 30,000 visitors within 10% using at most 1.5 kilobytes?
claims.not_checked: counts beyond 30,000 visitors, or the paper's 2% figure at a billion items

claims.name: jump-hash
claims.plain: Jump consistent hash moves only about 1 key in 11 when 10 buckets become 11, with nothing stored.
claims.paper: A Fast, Minimal Memory, Consistent Hash Algorithm
claims.quote: jump consistent hash requires no storage, is faster, and does a better job of evenly dividing the key space among the buckets and of evenly dividing the workload when the number of buckets changes.
claims.paper_number: no storage, an even split, and few keys moved when buckets change
claims.locked: place 100,000 keys in 10 buckets, then 11: between 8.2% and 10.0% move, all to the new bucket, the fullest bucket at most 5% over the mean, nothing stored
claims.question: Does jump consistent hash move only about 1 key in 11 when 10 buckets become 11?
claims.not_checked: bucket counts other than 10 and 11, or the paper's claim that it is faster

claims.name: xor-filter
claims.plain: An xor filter answers set membership with under 0.5% false positives in at most 10 bits per key, where a Bloom filter of that size cannot.
claims.paper: Xor Filters: Faster and Smaller Than Bloom and Cuckoo Filters
claims.quote: We find that xor filters can be faster than Bloom and cuckoo filters while using less memory.
claims.paper_number: less memory than a Bloom filter for the same answers
claims.locked: hold 50,000 keys, miss none, say yes to under 0.5% of 200,000 others, in at most 10 bits per key
claims.question: Does an xor filter give under 0.5% false positives in at most 10 bits per key?
claims.not_checked: speed, which the paper also claims, or the smaller xor+ variant

claims.name: morris-counter
claims.plain: A Morris counter counts 100,000 events within 10% in a 12-bit register, where an exact count needs 17 bits.
claims.quote: Storing a counter incremented N times would naively consume O(log N) bits of memory. In 1978 Morris described the very first streaming algorithm: the "Morris Counter".
claims.paper_number: far fewer bits than an exact count
claims.locked: count 100,000 events within 10% in at least 19 of 20 runs, in a register of at most 12 bits
claims.question: Does a Morris counter count 100,000 events within 10% in a 12-bit register?
claims.not_checked: the paper's own new algorithm or its lower bound: only the Morris counter it describes
